method: On the same disposable task ('ZZ probe detail' in both apps), before every keystroke the focused editor's current text was asserted to be exactly the task's own title. Tested: (0) activate editing with no changes, then Escape -- expect no confirmation; (1) type one character, click Cancel; (2) type one character (fresh activation), press Escape; (3) type one character (fresh activation), click far outside the modal. For each, recorded whether a confirmation appeared (role/title/body/buttons verbatim), then resolved it (Discard) before the next attempt.

noChangeCase.verdict: MATCH -- neither app asks anything when there are no unsaved changes.

attempt1_cancelButton.verdict: MATCH on title, body and button labels verbatim. role differs (dialog vs alertdialog) -- per instructions this is meologue's own decision and is recorded, not counted as a difference.

attempt2_escapeKey.verdict: MATCH -- Escape with unsaved changes triggers the same confirmation as Cancel in both apps.

afterClickingDiscard.note: Clicking Discard when the confirmation was triggered by an outside click closed the ENTIRE detail modal, not just the edit -- the outside click's original intent (leave the task) completed once the discard was confirmed.
Clicking Discard after an outside-click trigger only discarded the edit; the detail modal itself stayed open.

attempt3_clickOutsideModal.verdict: DIFFERS -- both apps show the identical confirmation text for an outside click, but resolving it with Discard has a different scope: Todoist closes the whole modal (the outside click's own action completes), meologue keeps the modal open (only the edit is discarded). This is a real, newly-observed difference, not previously in the ledger's DET-15 note.

escapeInsideConfirmation.method: With the confirmation open (from the Cancel-button trigger), pressed Escape once and recorded whether only the confirmation closed, whether the edit and its draft text survived, and whether the whole detail modal closed.

todoist.note: Confirmation closed; editing resumed with the draft ('ZZ probe detailX') still in place and focus back on the Task name editor; the detail modal itself never closed.

after.activeElementText: (whole app text -- focus fell back to document body, not the title editor)
after.draftVisibleInDialog: ZZ probe detailX (Cancel/Save buttons still present, confirming editing is still active)

meologue.note: Confirmation closed; the edit form remained active with its draft text intact and Cancel/Save still showing; the detail modal itself never closed. Focus landed on the document body rather than back on the Task name editor -- a minor difference from Todoist's behavior of returning focus to the editor.

escapeInsideConfirmation.verdict: MATCH on the required behavior (confirmation closes, draft and edit survive, modal stays open). Minor difference: Todoist returns keyboard focus to the Task name editor after the Escape; meologue does not return focus to any specific editable element.

clickDiscardAfterCancelTrigger.verdict: MATCH -- clicking Discard (after a Cancel-button or Escape-key trigger) ends editing, discards the draft, and leaves the modal open in both apps.

overallVerdict.note: The core ask (Cancel/Escape/outside-click all raise the same 'Discard unsaved changes?' confirmation with identical title/body/buttons; no-change Cancel/Escape ask nothing; Escape inside the confirmation closes only the confirmation and preserves the draft) is now satisfied in meologue -- this was the flow-4/5 defect (#14, no guard at all) and it is fixed. The one real difference found this round: after an OUTSIDE-CLICK-triggered confirmation, clicking Discard closes the whole modal in Todoist but only ends editing in meologue (attempt3_clickOutsideModal above). meologue's alertdialog role (vs Todoist's dialog role) is recorded per instructions but not counted as a difference.
